goal_text: (Reused from sequential_013) A chemist needs 120 liters of a 25% acid solution. She has a 40% acid solution and a 10% acid solution available. How many liters of each should she mix?
ground_truth: Let x = liters of 40% solution. Equation: 0.40x + 0.10(120-x) = 0.25*120. 0.40x + 12 - 0.10x = 30. 0.30x = 18. x = 60 liters of 40%; 120-60=60 liters of 10%.
